### Observed differences

- Activity A32 appears less often in the later window: its mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.0 to about 0.7, and the share of traces containing it fell from about 57 in 100 to about 43 in 100 [OCC001].
- Repetition of A32 also became less common: traces in which it recurs fell from about 26 in 100 to about 19 in 100 [OCC001].
- Both profiles rest on a substantial number of traces (113 before and 85 after, out of 200 each), and the difference is larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data; A32's occurrence is the only item in the evidence [OCC001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one control-flow item (the decrease in A32's occurrence) qualified, while about 0.3 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so this single difference — even with an empirical strength near 0.995 — is what an unchanged process typically produces and may reflect sampling variation or a rare variant rather than a behavioural change [OCC001].

- control_flow: 60 units tested, 1 item, 0.3 expected without change.
- time: 18 units tested, 0 items, 0.009 expected.

Evidence: one item, OCC001, CF_OCC for activity A32.

Before: mean occurrences per trace 1.025, trace participation 0.565 (about 57 in 100 traces), recurrence support 0.26.
After: mean occurrences 0.7, participation 0.425 (about 43 in 100 traces), recurrence support 0.19.

Differences: mean occurrences -0.325, participation -0.14, recurrence -0.07. Observed change 0.325. Empirical strength ~0.995 (about 995 of 1000 reference comparisons smaller).

Support: before 113 traces (containing A32), after 85 traces. Both windows have decent support (113/200, 85/200).

Judging: The screening comparison: control_flow family has 1 item vs 0.3 expected. That's the same order of magnitude — one item when fewer than one is expected is what an unchanged process typically produces. Per instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So despite empirical strength 0.995, we have 1 control-flow item vs 0.3 expected, and 0 time items vs 0.009 expected. Total 1 item vs 0.31 expected. This is exactly the "one item when fewer than one is expected" case → Insufficient evidence.

So the answer: Support level: Insufficient evidence.

Observed differences: In the later window, activity A32 appears less often: mean occurrences per trace dropped from about 1.0 to 0.7; the share of traces containing A32 fell from about 57 in 100 to about 43 in 100; recurrence (traces with multiple occurrences, presumably) fell from 26% to 19%. Empirical strength ~0.995 — unusual for random splits, but a single item.

Time family: no items.

Inference: Insufficient evidence. "The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process."
